title: Warm-index task workflow import and dedupe retrieval
query: import tasks duplicate normalized title project validation deterministic id

expectedFacts.text: importTasks validates normalized task titles and project ids before inserting records.
importTasks skips duplicates when a task with the same normalized title already exists in the same project.
New imported tasks still receive deterministic ids such as task-1 and task-2 from the shared store sequence.

answerKey.notes: Cross-module retrieval spanning the import service, validation, and store logic.

notes: v0.5.1 warm-index seed case grounded in the existing task-workflow-import-dedup behavior.

title: Warm-index create task with project metadata
query: create task validate project title priority tags normalize tags deterministic id

expectedFacts.text: createTask validates the title with validateTaskTitle, which collapses whitespace and rejects an empty title with "Task title must not be empty."
createTask validates the projectId with validateProjectId and throws "Unknown project id: <id>" when the store has no such project, before the task is stored.
Tags are normalized with normalizeTags (trimmed, lowercased, empty values dropped, de-duplicated, and sorted) before the task is stored.
TaskWorkflowStore.createTask assigns the id with createDeterministicId("task", sequence) from the store's shared incrementing sequence, producing ids such as task-1 and task-2.
A newly created task is stored with completed set to false.

answerKey.notes: Cross-module: the create service composes validation, the store, and the deterministic id utility.

notes: v0.5.1 warm-index medium case for task creation.

title: Warm-index idempotent task completion
query: complete task by id idempotent completedAt unknown task

expectedFacts.text: completeTask(store, taskId) changes one task by id through TaskWorkflowStore.updateTask.
The first completion sets completed to true and completedAt to "2026-02-01T00:00:00.000Z".
When the task is already completed the updater returns it unchanged, so completing it again does not rewrite completedAt.
An unknown task id throws "Unknown task id: <id>" from TaskWorkflowStore.updateTask.

answerKey.notes: Localized: the behavior lives in one service plus the store update primitive.

title: Warm-index composite task filtering
query: filter tasks project completed priority tag text query ordering

expectedFacts.text: filterTasks keeps a task only when it satisfies every supplied TaskFilter field; fields that are not supplied do not filter.
The projectId filter requires task.projectId to equal the requested project id.
The completed filter compares the boolean when defined, priority must match exactly, and the tag is trimmed and lowercased before checking task.tags.
The query is trimmed and lowercased and matched as a substring of the lowercased title, notes, and tags joined with spaces.
filterTasks only reads store.listTasks(), which returns task copies sorted by task id, and returns the matches in that order without mutating the store.

answerKey.notes: Cross-module: filter semantics depend on the TaskFilter model and store listing order.

notes: v0.5.1 warm-index medium case for composite filtering.

title: Warm-index workflow project summary

byProject holds total, completed, and open counts for every project returned by store.listProjects(), including zero counts for projects without tasks, plus any task projectId not registered as a project.
highPriorityOpenTitles lists the titles of tasks that are not completed and have priority "high".
summarizeTasks reads copies from store.listTasks() and store.listProjects() and does not mutate stored tasks.

title: Warm-index broad task workflow architecture map
query: explain task creation import duplicate filtering completion summary validation store workflow

expectedFacts.text: Both the createTask service and importTasks store new tasks through TaskWorkflowStore.createTask, sharing its deterministic task id sequence.

importTasks validates each item with validateImportInput and skips duplicates found by TaskWorkflowStore.findDuplicate (same project and normalized title), recording their ids in skippedDuplicates; plain task creation does not deduplicate.
filterTasks reads store.listTasks() and returns matching tasks without changing workflow state.
completeTask changes a single task by id through TaskWorkflowStore.updateTask.
summarizeTasks aggregates counts from the current tasks and projects held by the store.

forbiddenWrongClaims: importTasks calls the createTask service to insert imported tasks.
answerKey.notes: Deliberately wide-scope negative control spanning every workflow service; it is not expected to fit a small localized context.

title: Warm-index task analytics health label retrieval
query: completion rate stale tasks quality label health report analytics snapshot

expectedFacts.text: The analytics snapshot computes completionRate as completedTasks divided by totalTasks times 100, rounded to two decimals.
Stale tasks count only open tasks whose updated day is at least ten days behind the current day.
The Python quality layer maps metrics to healthy, watch, or risk labels based on completion rate and stale task thresholds.
The Python report writer emits one line per project with the quality label plus completion, open, and stale counts.

answerKey.notes: Cross-module retrieval spanning TypeScript snapshot building and Python quality reporting.

notes: v0.5.1 warm-index seed case grounded in the existing task-analytics-health-label behavior.

title: Warm-index TypeScript analytics snapshot
query: analytics snapshot project completion rate stale tasks average story points task store

expectedFacts.text: For each project from ProjectStore.list(), buildAnalyticsSnapshot loads the project's tasks with listTasksByProject (AnalyticsTaskStore.list() filtered by projectId) and records totalTasks, completedTasks, and openTasks as totalTasks minus completedTasks.
completionRate is completedTasks divided by totalTasks times 100, rounded to two decimals with Math.round(value * 100) / 100.
staleTasks counts only incomplete tasks whose currentDay minus updatedDay is at least STALE_DAY_THRESHOLD (10).
A project with no tasks gets zero counts, completionRate 0, and averageStoryPoints 0; otherwise averageStoryPoints is the mean story points rounded to two decimals.
The snapshot totals sum totalTasks, completedTasks, openTasks, and staleTasks across the per-project snapshots.

answerKey.notes: Cross-module: the snapshot service composes the task-listing service, the task store, and the snapshot model.

notes: v0.5.1 warm-index large case for the TypeScript analytics snapshot.

title: Warm-index deterministic project leaderboard
query: project leaderboard completion rate stale tasks tie break project id ranking

expectedFacts.text: buildProjectLeaderboard sorts a copy of snapshot.projects by completionRate in descending order.
Ties on completionRate are broken by staleTasks in ascending order.
Remaining ties are broken by projectId in ascending localeCompare order.
Each line is formatted as "<rank>. <projectId> (<completionRate>% complete, <staleTasks> stale)" with ranks starting at 1.

answerKey.notes: Localized: the ranking rule lives in one reporting function over the ProjectSnapshot model.

title: Warm-index Python parser and project metrics
query: parse task rows calculate project metrics completion open stale story points

expectedFacts.text: parse_task_rows converts each row into a TaskRecord with task_id and project_id as str, completed as bool, and story_points and updated_day as int.
calculate_project_metrics groups tasks by project_id and returns one ProjectMetrics per project in sorted project_id order.
open_tasks is total_tasks minus completed_tasks, and stale_tasks counts incomplete tasks whose current_day minus updated_day is at least STALE_DAY_THRESHOLD (10).
completion_rate is round((completed / total) * 100, 2), or 0.0 when a project has no tasks.
average_story_points is the mean story_points rounded with round(..., 2), or 0.0 when a project has no tasks.

answerKey.notes: Cross-module: parsing, the record models, and metric calculation live in separate Python modules.

notes: v0.5.1 warm-index large case for Python parsing and metrics.

title: Warm-index Python analytics report pipeline
query: pipeline parse rows project metrics quality label health report

expectedFacts.text: build_report_from_rows(rows, current_day) first parses the rows with parse_task_rows.
The parsed tasks go to calculate_project_metrics(tasks, current_day), and the resulting metrics go to build_health_report.
build_health_report calls determine_quality_label for each metric, which returns empty, healthy, watch, or risk from total_tasks, completion_rate, and stale_tasks thresholds.

The report is one line per project, "<project_id>: <label> | completion=<rate>% | open=<n> | stale=<n>", joined by newlines in sorted project_id order, so fixed rows and current_day produce the same output.
pipeline.py only composes parse_task_rows, calculate_project_metrics, and build_health_report; quality rules stay in quality.py and are reached through reporting.

answerKey.notes: Cross-module: the pipeline composes parser, metrics, reporting, and (through reporting) quality modules.

notes: v0.5.1 warm-index large case for the Python report pipeline.

title: Warm-index broad TypeScript and Python analytics comparison
query: compare TypeScript and Python project analytics snapshot metrics quality reporting pipeline leaderboard

expectedFacts.text: The TypeScript side builds analytics snapshots with buildAnalyticsSnapshot and presents them through formatTaskHealthReport, which uses buildProjectLeaderboard for ranking.

The Python side parses rows (parse_task_rows), derives project metrics (calculate_project_metrics), assigns quality labels (determine_quality_label), and builds reports (build_health_report), composed by build_report_from_rows.
Both sides expose comparable per-project health evidence: total, completed, open, and stale task counts plus a completion rate rounded to two decimals, using a stale threshold of 10 days.
The TypeScript and Python code are independent parallel benchmark implementations, not a runtime TypeScript-to-Python call chain.
Neither implementation imports, spawns, or calls the other; TypeScript imports stay within ts/src and Python imports stay within the task_analytics package.

forbiddenWrongClaims: The TypeScript implementation invokes the Python analytics pipeline.
Python is a runtime backend for the TypeScript analytics implementation.
The TypeScript or Python implementation directly imports or calls the other.
answerKey.notes: Deliberately wide-scope negative control spanning both language implementations; it is not expected to fit a small localized context.

notes: v0.5.1 warm-index large broad-change negative control.
